definition: Reused from matrix-2026-10 (its definition in new_features.csv): in its primary use the form heads a nominal with a separate determiner before it (the few, the two, a dog, the rich). This is CGEL's first noun-typical dependent, 'certain determinatives' (ch. 5 §1 [2iii]). For the 139 forms, values are copied from new_feature_values.csv, NA read as n.

In its primary use, a restrictive pre-head AdjP modifies the nominal the form heads (good news, the lucky few, a huge lot of time). Non-restrictive adjectives (poor me, young Isaac Newton) are excluded; the exclamative lucky/poor/silly type has its own column (take_poor_lucky_silly_as_attrib_modifiers).
source: CGEL ch. 5 §1 [2iii]; ch. 6 §2 (adjectives aren't modified by adjectives)

definition: An integrated relative clause modifies the nominal the form heads (people who work, those who came, we who have read the report). Delayed relatives (Who do you know who...) don't count.
The form takes a complement other than a partitive of-phrase: an of-PP (a lot of people, a number of boys), another PP or clause (the fact that, proud of), or a than-phrase (more than ten).
source: Added by Claude, not on CGEL's lists: motivated by the quantity nouns' of-complements (CGEL pp. 349-350) and adjectives' complements (proud of)

definition: An NP headed by the form is the complement of a preposition (to the doctor, for some, to him). Dependent-only forms and nominative pronouns are n.
An NP headed by the form modifies an AdvP (a whole day late, much later, that quickly, the sooner).
An NP headed by the form modifies a PP (a mile under the sea, much before noon, all over the floor).
A post-head AdjP modifies the nominal the form heads (someone nice, the people present, those present, all present).
Graded by analytic more and most (more useful, more numerous).

Modified by a degree or evaluative -ly adverb (remarkably happy, surprisingly few, considerably more); the approximators (almost, nearly, hardly, approximately) have their own columns and are excluded.
source: CGEL ch. 6 §2 [1iii]; p. 538 (the modifier test: nouns 'are modified by adjectives, not adverbs')
